bullets.title: Semis sell off 5% on AI ARR miss; Anthropic eclipses OpenAI in Q2 revenue
bullets.body: The SOX fell ~5% and Nasdaq -1.3% on Tuesday as Anthropic's Q2 ARR came in at ~$65B vs. $75-80B market expectations, triggering a momentum de-grossing event described as one of the 10 largest post-ChatGPT selloffs. Simultaneously, OpenAI reported only 18% QoQ revenue growth to $6.7B while Anthropic more than doubled to $11.6B and achieved profitability—a stark reversal of the perceived competitive order. Goldman noted 20+ one-day 5% selloffs in the High Beta Momentum basket this year vs. five in prior years.

bullets.title: Long-end yields near cycle highs; 30-year hits 5.31%, highest since 2007
bullets.body: The 10-year Treasury reached ~4.70-4.75% and the 30-year briefly touched 5.34%, highest since 2007, driven by heavy AI-related corporate IG supply (on pace for $1.9T in 2026, nearly double 2025), fiscal deterioration ($600B in new national debt since July 1), and Hormuz-related oil pass-through inflation risks. Hedgeye's CPI Nowcast models Headline CPI at 3.43% in 3Q26 and 3.61% in 4Q26; disinflationary backdrop not expected until 2Q27. The 10s-2s curve has steepened to +53bps from +25bps in late June.

bullets.title: Iran-UAE escalation: ballistic missiles, Hormuz near-closure, Trump halts talks
bullets.body: Iran fired two ballistic missiles at UAE (both intercepted), UAE severed all trade and financial ties with Iran, and Strait of Hormuz logged just six vessel crossings on Tuesday. Trump simultaneously ordered all US envoy talks with Iran halted, pivoting to a long-term economic strangulation strategy. Brent settled at $91.02/bbl (+0.17%) and WTI at $84.94 (+0.52%); diesel crack spreads hit $102/bbl with US reserves at 23-year lows. One analyst flagged a potential spurious-but-worth-watching correlation between Hormuz tanker traffic and 10-year real yields.

bullets.title: $4.2tn options expiry Aug 21; NVDA earnings Aug 26 the key near-term catalyst
bullets.body: Citi flags $4.2tn notional open interest expiring Thursday—the largest August expiry in recent history—split $2.7tn indices, $659bn ETFs, $844bn single-stocks. Options volumes had been muted for two weeks. NVDA's +16% pre-earnings rally (largest since May 2025) and implied ~4.9% earnings-day move (near 10-year lows) set up an asymmetric setup; Citi recommends SMH Nov-26 $600 calls as the cleaner expression. Separately, Citi raises its NVDA Jul-Q revenue estimate to $93B vs. Street $92B on B300/Rubin ramp.

bullets.title: Hedge fund flows: largest 3-week US equity buying since March 2020; semis re-risk
bullets.body: Goldman Prime reports US equities net bought for three straight weeks—the largest 3-week buying pace since March 2020—led by TMT/hyperscalers and semis. Short exposure in US Macro Products fell to lowest YTD levels. Despite this, Tuesday saw -1.8 SD net selling of AI Winners and -3.0 SD in hardware, 90% driven by long reduction rather than short covering. Mag7 net allocation sits at ~18% vs. June low of 14%. China most net bought in Asia but allocation still near 5-year lows.

bullets.title: FOMC minutes due today (14:00 ET); Jackson Hole (Aug 27-29) and Warsh speech next key macro events
bullets.body: July FOMC minutes release at 2pm ET is today's main event alongside a $16B 20-year bond auction. JPM flagged that bond traders are already hedging against any dovish Fed pivot by mid-2027. Fed Governor Warsh expected to outline a framework reshaping speech at Jackson Hole Aug 27-29—a potential regime-change signal for markets currently running with a structurally steeper curve.

bullets.title: Pennsylvania data center executive order creates new regulatory headwind for AI infrastructure
bullets.body: Governor Shapiro signed an executive order removing all AI data center proposals from PA's fast-track permitting, mandating GRID standards (energy affordability, environmental, workforce requirements), and banning NDAs for project communications. Goldman assessed limited near-term impact on well-capitalized developers but speculative projects face higher hurdles. CRWV fell -3.5% and IREN -2.4% pre-market; TLN dropped ~11% intraday. Multiple sources note regulatory fatigue spreading across states (TX, OH, GA, PA).

bullets.title: AI sovereignty becomes $860B structural theme; US-China tech decoupling extends to cloud and models
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley frames US AI sovereignty as a $860B annual capex opportunity, with federal support expected for domestic build-out and tighter China controls extending beyond chips to cloud access, model distribution, and procurement. Sovereign AI reinforces rather than undermines the capex cycle by extending duration. China simultaneously pursues indigenous capability, while Europe faces financing and scale challenges. The AI Sovereignty & Semi Localization thematic cohort is among the fastest-growing with premium valuations.

bullets.title: Memory upcycle intact; HBM shortage pivots AI build-out from scale-up to scale-out
bullets.body: Citi Peter Lee notes the memory upcycle is sustained by tight inventories and strong KV-cache demand. NVDA's Vera Rubin CMX architecture requires ~576 enterprise SSDs (9.6PB) per config, driving TLC NAND demand; Samsung is mass-producing 16TB PM1763 enterprise SSDs for Rubin deployments. Micron reportedly unable to meet more than half of customer demand. JPM notes HBM shortage is constraining NVDA/Google GPU and TPU production, pushing architecture from scale-up to scale-out. Morgan Stanley separately warns DDR4 prices will jump 50% in Q3 as chipmakers shift capacity to HBM.

bullets.title: KEYSIGHT beats with record $2.1B orders; AI wireline surpasses wireless for first time
bullets.body: KEYS F3Q revenue hit $1.85B (+31% YoY organic), beating Street estimates; orders reached $2.09B (+52% YoY). Commercial Comms grew 56% YoY with wireline orders >2x YoY—wireline revenue exceeded wireless for the first time. F4Q guidance of $1.93-1.95B was at the high end of expectations. FY26 EPS growth ~60% at midpoint. Morgan Stanley, Citi, JPM, and Goldman all raised PTs ($400-$452 range) maintaining Buy/OW ratings; positioned as lower-volatility, architecture-agnostic AI infrastructure play.

bullets.title: Retail impulses diverge: TGT strong, LOW cuts guidance, TJX mixed on Marmaxx
bullets.body: Target posted +3.8% Q2 comps (vs. +2.4% est.) with digital +8.7% and raised FY26 EPS to $9.90-$10.90 including tariff refunds; stock +56% YTD. Lowe's cut FY26 revenue guidance to $92B (from $94B) with comps now flat vs. prior flat-to-+2%, citing persistent DIY weakness; HD outperformed LOW US comps by ~110bps. TJX posted +4% total comps but the key Marmaxx division grew only +1% (vs. +2-3% expected), limiting the upside path; Citi and UBS both note 3Q/4Q EPS guidance below Street is a headwind.

bullets.title: Asia markets hit hard: KOSPI -5.8%, Nikkei -3.4% on semi selloff and rate pressure
bullets.body: South Korea's KOSPI activated the sidecar circuit breaker as Samsung and SK Hynix each fell ~7%, with the broader KOSPI down 5.4-5.8%. Japan's Nikkei fell 2.6-3.4% and Taiwan's Taiex -1.3%; China's CSI 300 dropped 2.9% (2 standard deviations). The selloff was attributed to the US semiconductor rout, rising bond yields globally, and elevated crude prices from Hormuz uncertainty. JPM brought forward its BoJ rate hike call to September (December thereafter) with 3 further hikes expected in 2027.

bullets.title: NVDA H200 chips allowed into China for ByteDance and Tencent; ~10K units each
bullets.body: China eased restrictions on Nvidia H200 chips, with ByteDance and Tencent each receiving approximately 10,000 units. The move reflects escalating competitive dynamics in the global AI race and was reported by the Financial Times. Multiple sources confirm the development and note China's Foreign Ministry simultaneously opposed US pressure to 'choose sides' on AI geopolitics.

bullets.title: US-Canada tariff tension: 50% tariffs paused 3 days; deal at 50-50 odds
bullets.body: Trump paused the 50% Canada tariffs for three days subject to a deal, citing progress in negotiations including potential Keystone XL pipeline revival. Canadian PM Carney said 'substantial progress' was made but 'more work needed.' Autos remain the key sticking point; US officials privately assessed deal probability at 50% or lower before the deadline. USD dropped 0.2% vs CAD on the news.

bullets.title: UK July CPI beats at 2.9% YoY; BoE supercore services accelerates to 4.2% annualized
bullets.body: UK headline CPI rose to 2.9% YoY in July (matching consensus), but core held at 2.6% with a 0.3% MoM surprise. BoE's supercore services measure rose 0.5% MoM SA (fastest since December), with annualized change up to 4.2%. JPM's base case is a November BoE rate hike but acknowledges the MPC may lack sufficient evidence by then. Headline CPI on track to reach ~3.5% by year-end per energy price assumptions.

bullets.title: Reddit citations in ChatGPT collapse 86%; OpenAI pauses largest frontier RL run
bullets.body: Reddit's share of ChatGPT citations fell from 3.8% to below 0.5% (86% drop) after August 8, raising questions about the value of its licensing agreement with OpenAI. Separately, OpenAI paused its largest planned frontier RL run to apply strict cyber safeguards after determining its Astra models have 'critical cyber capability.' OpenAI is also updating its safety rules post-Hugging Face developments.

bullets.title: Broad market breadth deteriorating despite index near highs; Hindenburg Omen triggers
bullets.body: NYSE is showing 3x more 52-week lows than highs—the last comparable divergence was December 14, 2021—while SPY sits ~2% from all-time highs. The Hindenburg Omen has triggered 15 times in the past 3 months (prior record of 16 was followed by a 19% drawdown). S&P price/breadth divergence is on pace for a record frequency. Hedgeye's risk range for the S&P is 7,652-7,811 with a bullish trend signal but notes UST 10yr in Bullish Trend as a headwind for housing and growth.

bullets.title: Piper Sandler: consumer credit conditions easing, supporting 3% real spending growth
bullets.body: Piper Sandler sees improving lending standards and loan demand through Q3, with household income expectations edging higher and fears of missed payments declining. The firm models 3% real consumer spending growth in 2026, with goods and durables benefiting most from easing credit. Student loan delinquencies have declined; subprime auto delinquencies at record highs but the cohort's share of total auto debt is historically low. Sticky inflation remains a headwind for low-income consumers.

bullets.title: AI capex credit crowding out Treasuries; hyperscaler IG debt on track to double to $659B
bullets.body: Investment-grade supply is tracking toward $1.9T in 2026, nearly double 2025's pace and exceeding the 2020 record of $1.66T, driven largely by hyperscaler AI data center financing. Hyperscaler IG debt is projected to grow from $288B to $659B in two years—approaching the debt levels of the big six US banks. One strategist noted that 100bps in yield today has the destructive power of 400bps in the 1990s due to lower rate regimes.

bullets.title: LME copper stocks jump 35,650 tons; gold overtakes Treasuries as top central bank reserve
bullets.body: LME copper on-warrant stocks jumped 35,650 tons—the largest single-day increase since early 2024—a potential signal of weakening industrial demand. Separately, gold has overtaken US Treasuries as the world's largest central bank reserve asset, as gold gained 0.8%+ on the session. Hedgeye recommends short USD/long gold positioning with USD in a bearish trend.
